races.paceDynamic: Laravie is the lone front-runner in this three-runner contest over 1m6f at Yarmouth on good-to-firm ground, and with no rivals willing or able to challenge for the lead, she will control every fraction from the gate. Racing prominently by style and carrying a visor, Laravie arrives on a hat-trick of wins over similar staying trips and will set a measured, uncontested tempo that could be deceptively steady through the early stages. Both Betelgeuse and Captain Brett are hold-up horses who will sit in behind and rely on a strong enough gallop to bring their finishing kicks into play. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or prominent racer who can dictate and conserve energy at a controlled pace — the hold-up pair need Laravie to stretch things out, but she holds every card in setting the terms she prefers.

races.paceDynamic: Rocking Ends is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f sprint at Yarmouth on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine rival willing to press him for the lead, he is set to control a measured, sustainable gallop from the gates. Havana Blast is the only other prominent-style horse and is more likely to track than challenge for the lead, meaning Rocking Ends can dictate without being pressured. The hold-up contingent of Twilight Calls, Michaela's Boy, Law Of Average, and Cressida Wildes all share the rear of the field, though Law Of Average and Cressida Wildes are true hold-up types redistributed into the midfield picture on the map — the field holds more closers than the race shape comfortably accommodates at the back, and Twilight Calls and Michaela's Boy are the most likely to genuinely occupy those rearward berths. An uncontested lead on fast ground over an undemanding flat five furlongs strongly favours the prominent and front-running profile — a horse that can control tempo and outstay rivals from the front is ideally placed, with hold-up runners needing either an overly brisk pace or a well-timed split that this shape may simply not deliver.

watchPoints.text: Rocking Ends exits the stalls cleanly — if he misses the break in a small field of six, the entire race shape collapses and hold-up horses inherit a far more live chance.
Twilight Calls and Michaela's Boy are the genuine closers; watch whether either can find a clear passage in a six-runner race where the field may fan wide early and leave limited ground to make up.

Law Of Average's last two wins came on Good and Firm — if the going is riding faster than the official Good to Firm assessment, his class and recent form make him a sharper threat than his redistributed map position implies.

Havana Blast's course and trip record on non-Standard surfaces is limited (4 from 9 on similar going); if he fails to travel comfortably tracking Rocking Ends, the prominent profile in this race is thinly represented and the race becomes more one-dimensional.

With only six runners on a straight flat five furlongs, a wide draw could grant any hold-up horse a rails-hugging or clear-air run without being blocked — check stall positions and early race positioning once the handlers release them.

races.paceDynamic: Charlie's Choice is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressurer likely to challenge for the lead, will be allowed to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in a genuine position — King's Hand and Nicator — or those proven closers with the tactical speed to pounce off a modest, uncontested gallop, rather than hold-up horses who need a truly searching pace to reel in the leaders.

races.paceDynamic: Knights Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth's flat mile, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested tempo without any genuine pace rival to force him into an early duel. Behind him, Cancan In The Rain, Sea Suite, and Red Hat Eagle are natural prominent types who will compete for the early positions just off the leader, creating a compact early order but not a truly pressured gallop. The field holds more prominent-minded horses than can all slot naturally into those early positions — Gorgeous Mr George, Kalamunda, and Hitched are genuine pace-biased or hold-up types redistributed on the map, meaning real scrimmaging for positions two through five is probable, with Knights Gold, Cancan In The Rain, and Sea Suite most likely to actually secure their preferred slots. A lone, relaxed front-runner on fast ground over a flat mile at Yarmouth creates a rail-hugging, controlled tempo that classically suits hold-up finishers who can track and quicken in the straight, or a prominent horse with the engine to maintain their position and outstay rivals once the pace lifts — the tactical verdict favours genuine hold-up horses who can draft off the steady tempo and unleash a sustained late run.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Encore's 76-day absence is a concern, but if Chapple-Hyam has him spot-on for this Yarmouth return over the exact trip of his last win, he is the most naturally suited profile to the anticipated pace shape and any sign of freshness in the paddock should be noted.

The scrimmage for prominent positions early on — between Cancan In The Rain, Sea Suite, Red Hat Eagle, and the redistributed Gorgeous Mr George and Kalamunda — could create a slightly uneven early pace, which would be the key race-shape-altering event to watch for in the opening two furlongs.

Cancan In The Rain's 258-day absence makes her a significant watch at the start and in the early stages — if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness or fails to stride out prominently, her scenario (B) collapses and the weight shifts firmly back to scenario A.

Knights Gold's STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) deserves monitoring — if he finds himself pressed by Sea Suite or Cancan In The Rain off a fast break, the uncontested gallop evaporates and the probability profile shifts meaningfully toward hold-up horses arriving late.

Influential's trainer Roger Varian is 5/19 in the 14-day window — the second-strongest yard stat in the race — making this horse worth tracking through the early furlongs to see whether Robbie Downey commits to a closer's run or attempts to edge closer than usual.
